title: AI-supported first consultation preparation in oncology: a real-world clinical usability study
desc: Large Language Models (LLMs) may support clinicians by facilitating information management, but their usability in real-world oncology practice remains understudied. This study evaluated the workflow performance of Artificial Intelligence-based First Consultation Preparation (AI-FCP), generating structured summaries from unstructured clinical documentation, co-created with end users. In a prospective single‑group pre‑post design, nine clinicians completed a person-level baseline, followed by 33 consultations with AI-FCP. Case numbers varied by clinic scheduling and enrollment timing, potentially introducing survivorship bias. Usability was evaluated using validated questionnaires and study-specific instruments. Post AI-FCP, overall perceived workload (NASA-TLX) was 28.9% lower than baseline (Hodges-Lehmann estimate difference −12.3; 95% CI –21.7 to –3.3), with self-reported average time savings of 3.26 min (SD = 2.65) per case. Preparation succeeded in 84.9% of consultations; 63.6% of summaries were complete. These exploratory findings suggest clinicians perceived lower workload and reported improved workflow efficiency with AI-FCP. Further research is needed to determine generalizability.

title: Performance uncertainty in medical image analysis: A large-scale investigation of confidence intervals
desc: Publication date: February 2027 Source: Medical Image Analysis, Volume 116 Author(s): Pascaline André, Charles Heitz, Evangelia Christodoulou, Annika Reinke, Carole H. Sudre, Michela Antonelli, Patrick Godau, M. Jorge Cardoso, Antoine Gilson, Sophie Tezenas du Montcel, Gaël Varoquaux, Lena Maier-Hein, Olivier Colliot

title: Machine Learning in Dementia Research: Trends, Biomarkers, Prediction Goals, and Data Modalities.
desc: [Brain and behavior] Machine learning (ML) is increasingly used in dementia research for diagnosis, early detection, prognosis, biomarker characterization, and disease phenotyping. This study aimed to provide a bibliometric and thematic overview of ML applications in dementia, emphasizing biological mechanisms, prediction goals, data modalities, collaborative networks, and emerging computational approaches. A title-field search of the Web of Science Core Collection identified 3,833 records related to ML and dementia. After restricting publications to 2000 onward and excluding non-analytic document types, 3,479 records were included in the bibliometric analysis. A subset of 3,223 original articles was used for thematic analyses. Publication trends, authorship, institutional collaboration, keywords, biomarker themes, ML objectives, data modalities, methods, shared research resources, and large language model (LLM) applications were evaluated. ML-related dementia research increased substantially over time. Diagnostic classification was the predominant ML objective (55.0%), followed by early detection or screening (10.3%), progression or cognitive-decline prediction (6.8%), and biomarker or feature discovery (4.7%). Structural magnetic resonance imaging was the most frequently identified modality (42.6%), followed by clinical or cognitive data (22.4%), positron emission tomography/single photon emission computerized tomography (10.3%), and genetic or genomic data (10.2%). Prominent biological themes included hippocampal measures, amyloid/Aβ, electroencephalogram, tau/p-tau, and cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers. Institutional networks showed distinct international collaboration clusters and frequent use of shared infrastructures. Transformer-based and LLM approaches emerged in recent years. ML research in dementia has expanded beyond diagnostic neuroimaging toward multimodal, biomarker, prognostic, and language model applications, although diagnostic classification and structural imaging remain dominant. Emphasis on biological integration, longitudinal validation, and clinical translation are needed.

title: CucurbitAgent: An AI agent for exploring cucurbit multi-omics resources
desc: Functional genomics in crops increasingly depends on integrating information from an extensive literature and heterogeneous multi-omics datasets. Large language models (LLMs) offer a powerful approach to synthesizing these resources and revealing hidden connections across datasets; however, they frequently hallucinate, producing plausible but unsupported claims, when responding to gene-specific queries. Here, we present CucurbitAgent, an AI research agent for functional genomics in the Cucurbitaceae, a major family of horticultural crops. CucurbitAgent integrates multi-omics resources from nine cultivated cucurbit species and more than 18,000 publications, encompassing approximately 256,000 genes, tissue-resolved expression profiles, over 16 million natural genetic variants, and roughly 242,000 predicted protein structures with more than 14 million predicted binding-site residue annotations. Responses link retrieved evidence to source records, including gene entries, expression measurements, structural predictions, and literature passages. On a curated benchmark of 50 tasks assessed by domain experts under blinded conditions, CucurbitAgent achieved an overall pairwise win rate of 96.0% against nine general-purpose LLMs, based on weighted scores for factual accuracy, completeness, relevance, and traceability. The platform is freely available at https://cucurbitagent.com and supports queries in 37 languages collectively spoken by an estimated 70% or more of the world's population. CucurbitAgent not only unifies evidence retrieval and interpretation but also reveals latent associations across datasets, helping researchers formulate testable hypotheses and substantially accelerating candidate-gene research. Its framework is readily transferable to other crops and, more broadly, provides a blueprint for building specialized agents in any domain.

title: Sycophantic AI, critical-feedback tolerance, and the case for productive friction in medical training
desc: Concerns about generative AI in medical training often focus on eroded reasoning and deskilling. Such competence-based accounts are incomplete. We identify a neglected casualty: critical-feedback tolerance (CFT), the capacity to receive disconfirming evaluative feedback and remain productively engaged. Affirmation-optimized systems may lower CFT undetectably, surfacing only under authentic critique. This conceptual Perspective defines CFT, differentiates it from six established constructs, specifies measurable facets, and states explicit refutation conditions.

title: AI-driven multi-omics biomarkers in precision breast cancer therapeutics: from discovery to clinical translation.
desc: [Frontiers in pharmacology] Breast cancer is biologically heterogeneous, yet conventional clinical decisions rely on static, single-marker proxies (ER, PR, HER2, and Ki-67) that capture only a narrow slice of tumor biology. This mini-review argues that AI-driven multi-omics biomarkers offer a valuable shift toward systems-level, model-derived probabilities integrating genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, metabolomic, and imaging information to explain and predict disease behavior more faithfully. We synthesize recent advances across three domains: (i) computational strategies for multi-omics integration, from classical penalized regression and ensemble learning to deep multimodal architectures and foundation-model embeddings; (ii) therapeutically relevant biomarker classes across tissue, liquid biopsy, and imaging modalities; and (iii) emerging pathways for embedding these biomarkers into clinical decision support. We highlight validation, interpretability, and robust handling of missing modalities as prerequisites for clinical trust, and outline how biomarker-driven trials, standardized reporting (e.g., TRIPOD + AI), and privacy-preserving data consortia can move AI-driven multi-omics biomarkers toward clinical and regulatory maturity.

title: Benchmarking Large Language Models for Assay-Aware Drug-Target Binding Affinity Prediction
desc: Machine learning models for molecular discovery often train on bioactivity data from heterogeneous assays, yet assay context is rarely explicitly represented. We investigate whether natural-language assay descriptions provide predictive information beyond molecular and protein representations. We develop ACL-DTI (Assay-aware Contrastive Learning-based Drug Target Interaction) and MAMMAL-AsAP, an assay-context extension of MAMMAL-DTI. Across five triplet-disjoint random splits, assay-aware models achieve competitive or improved performance over assay-agnostic baselines. Among the evaluated models, MAMMAL-AsAP achieves the highest (R^2) of 0.7198 +/- 0.0085. Masking experiments show that ACL-DTI is robust to incomplete assay descriptions, exhibiting the smallest reductions in R^2 among the evaluated models when masking the target name, assay technique, or both: 0.0228 +/- 0.0064, 0.0406 +/- 0.0113, and 0.0620 +/- 0.0190, respectively. These results indicate that assay descriptions contain predictive information not fully captured by molecular structures and protein sequences, and reveal architecture-dependent differences in how this information is exploited.

Automated differentiation for parkinsonism using clinical structural MRI: A multicenter study
desc: Multimodal research-grade magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans show potential for differentiating Parkinson’s disease (PD) from multiple system atrophy (MSA), but clinical translation is limited by cost, acquisition time, and processing burden. Here, we developed a T1-weighted structural MRI-based machine learning model to differentiate Parkinsonism and generalized it to routine anisotropic 2D clinical MRI. Using a multicenter cohort of 969 participants, we employed a hierarchical discovery–verification–translation framework. While a multimodal benchmark model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.98, our streamlined unimodal T1-Top20 model achieved an AUROC of 0.93 for multiclass discrimination (healthy controls, PD, MSA). For PD vs MSA, the frozen T1-Top20 model achieved a pooled AUROC of 0.88 in the external research-grade cohort ( n = 227) and identified 19 of 25 who phenoconverted from idiopathic rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder (iRBD) to PD. Importantly, the generalized model achieved a pooled AUROC of 0.84 in the clinical-MRI cohort (2D T1, n = 303), supporting its potential for clinical translation.

title: Artificial intelligence empowering the diagnosis and treatment of rotator cuff tears: A systematic review from image optimization to prognosis prediction.
desc: [Medicine] Artificial intelligence (AI) is being developed for image acquisition, quantitative tissue assessment, diagnosis, and clinical prediction in rotator cuff tears. The breadth of this literature and its methodological limitations have not been integrated across the complete care pathway. We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library from inception to July 5, 2026 for English-language original studies applying AI to rotator cuff-related reconstruction, segmentation or quantitative imaging, diagnosis or classification, anatomical measurement, or prognosis. Two reviewers screened reports and extracted study, data, model, validation, reference standard, and performance characteristics. Diagnostic accuracy studies were assessed with QUADAS-2 and prediction-model studies with PROBAST. Because clinical tasks, modalities, models, reference standards, and reported metrics were not sufficiently comparable, evidence was synthesized narratively rather than pooled statistically. Sixty-six reports were included: 35 diagnostic accuracy or classification studies, 20 segmentation or quantitative imaging studies, 9 prognosis or outcome prediction studies, 1 Magnetic Resonance Imaging reconstruction or image-optimization study, and 1 exploratory unsupervised-phenotyping study. Applications spanned Magnetic Resonance Imaging, radiography, ultrasound, computed tomography, clinical or multimodal data, motion video, and emerging sensing data. QUADAS-2 classified overall risk-of-bias as high in 27/36 diagnostic studies, unclear in 6/36, and low in 3/36. PROBAST classified all 8/8 completed prediction-model studies as high risk-of-bias; 1 protocol without model results was not rated. Promising internal performance was recurrent, but selection methods, imperfect or incompletely described reference standards, limited external validation, small or selected datasets, and analysis-stage weaknesses constrained clinical inference. AI has proof-of-concept value across rotator cuff imaging and decision support, but the current evidence does not establish routine clinical readiness or replacement of clinician judgment. Prospective multicenter studies, transparent reference standards, independent external validation, calibration and clinical-utility assessment, and standardized task-specific reporting are required.

title: BioMINTREL expands biological problem solving through cross-disciplinary representations
desc: Biological research agents often rely on familiar analytical methods, limiting the questions explored in existing data. We introduce BioMINTREL, an AI agent that finds methods from other disciplines and connects them to biological measurements. It can draw on relationships among datasets and complementary ideas from several methods to develop new questions and analyses. We evaluate it on BioMDC-Bench, which assesses 228 possible applications of computational methods to biological tasks. Compared with GPT-5.4 mini and Qwen3.6-35B, BioMINTREL improves F1 agreement with human experts by up to 45.3 percentage points and increases coverage of applications supported by studies published in subsequent years by up to 58.8 percentage points. Four case studies on real data go beyond previous analyses to reveal dose-specific variant effects, constraints on spatial cell communication and routes through perturbation-response states, and identify the sampling needed to test whether rare high-state cells predict later lineage size. These results highlight BioMINTREL's potential to expand questions in existing data and suggest directions for subsequent research.

Effectiveness of ecological momentary interventions for patients with cancer: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
desc: Symptom burden and impaired quality of life (QoL) are major challenges for patients with cancer. Ecological Momentary Interventions (EMIs) offer real-time, context-sensitive, and personalized support, enabling more precise management of patient needs. To explore the effectiveness of EMIs in improving symptoms and QoL in patients with cancer, a systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted. Following PRISMA 2020, a comprehensive search was conducted in nine databases from inception to December 8, 2025. The RoB 2 tool and GRADE were used to assess risk of bias and certainty of evidence, respectively. The R (version 4.4.1) and the “meta” package were used for statistical analysis. A total of 17 studies involving 4,160 randomized participants were included. The results suggested that EMIs may improve depression in patients with cancer, but were not associated with significant improvements in fatigue, pain severity, pain interference, sleep disturbance, anxiety, or QoL. Given the limited certainty and robustness of the available evidence, further adequately powered, allocation-concealed randomized controlled trials with blinded outcome assessment, where feasible, are needed to strengthen the evidence base for EMIs in oncology care.

title: Deep Learning-Based Automated Computed Tomography Classification of Posterior Malleolar Fractures for a Standardized Diagnostic Framework.
source: PubMed · Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
desc: [Journal of imaging informatics in medicine] Despite advances in computed tomography (CT)-based classification systems for posterior malleolar fractures (PMFs), diagnostic consistency remains limited because these systems are still highly dependent on the observer's experience. This study aimed to develop a deep learning-based automated model capable of classifying PMFs according to the Haraguchi, Mason-Molloy, and Bartoníček-Rammelt clasification systems using CT scans, and to compare the classification performance of different convolutional neural network architectures. Retrospectively collected preoperative CT data from 480 adult patients with PMFs were analyzed. A total of 2398 CT slices were independently classified by three orthopedic surgeons according to the three classification systems, and majority consensus was used as the reference standard. Anonymized DICOM images were evaluated using VGG-16, ResNet-101, and DenseNet-121 architectures. The dataset was divided into 60% training, 20% validation, and 20% testing subsets. Model performance was assessed using accuracy, sensitivity, precision, F1 score, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). The VGG-16 and ResNet-101 models demonstrated high classification performance in the Haraguchi and Mason-Molloy systems. In the VGG-16 model, AUC values exceeded 0.90 across most fracture subtypes, reaching particularly high levels in Haraguchi types I-III, Mason-Molloy types IIB and III, and Bartoníček-Rammelt type IV. Similarly, the ResNet-101 model achieved AUC values above 0.90 in most classes, with very high discriminative performance observed in selected subtypes. F1-scores were greater than 0.70 among most fracture categories and exceeded 0.80 in several, indicating strong and consistent classification performance. These findings demonstrate that deep learning-based automated CT classification of PMFs is feasible and diagnostically robust. The proposed framework may improve diagnostic consistency, reduce observer-dependent variability, and support standardized assessment of posterior malleolar fractures in clinical practice.

title: Focus investment on AI governance
AI做手术需海量临床数据支撑
A generalist model for diverse text-guided medical image synthesis
desc: Deep learning requires extensive data to achieve robust performance. However, data availability is often restricted in medicine due to patient privacy concerns. Synthetic data from medical image generative models present a possible solution to these challenges. Unfortunately, many models are often task-specific or trained on private datasets, limiting scalability and reproducibility. To address this, we introduce MediSyn: an open-access, generalist, text-guided latent diffusion model. MediSyn can generate images across 6 medical specialties and 10 imaging modalities, while being trained exclusively on public data. Our study provides several key contributions using MediSyn. First, we demonstrate that a generalist model can generate images of comparable quality to task-specific models across multiple specialties. Second, we show that this generalist approach is more computationally efficient than a suite of task-specific models. Third, we establish that a generalist model can produce realistic, text-aligned images across visually and medically distinct modalities. Fourth, we empirically demonstrate that these synthetic images are visually distinct from real images used in training. Finally, we show that a generalist model can produce images that improve classifier performance in data-limited settings across multiple specialties. Altogether, our findings highlight the potential of generalist image generative models to accelerate medical algorithmic research and development.

title: Tumor under forces: biophysical remodeling of tumor microenvironment and associated therapeutic opportunities.
desc: [Seminars in cancer biology] Tumors progress within a mechanically dynamic tumor microenvironment (TME), where extracellular matrix (ECM) stiffening, solid stress, and elevated interstitial fluid pressure remodel tumor cell and tumor-associated cell behavior. This TME-related mechanical remodeling often leads to tumor progression, metastasis and therapy resistance. In this review, we highlight recent advances in tumor mechanobiology, emphasizing how biophysical forces generated by cross-talk between tumor cells and tumor-associated cells precisely drive TME remodeling-ECM stiffening, hypoxia, leaky vasculature, invasion and therapy resistance-to support cancer progression. We discuss emerging interventions for selective tumor targeting that exploit the mechanical properties of the TME and biomechanical vulnerabilities of tumors and tumor-associated cells. Finally, this review explores the potential to leverage mechanobiological insights into the TME using New Approach Methodologies (NAMs), such as 3D bioprinted models and organ-on-chip platforms, coupled with AI-powered image analysis and modeling, to enable personalized cancer diagnosis and treatment.

title: How UCHealth navigates change management, tracks ROI for its AI deployments
京东健康与重医附一院战略签约，共建“心理康复与医疗智能体实验室”
A multi-stage validation framework for trustworthy large-scale clinical information extraction using large language models
desc: Large language models (LLMs) show promise for extracting clinically meaningful information from unstructured health records, yet real-world deployment is constrained by limited scalable, trustworthy validation approaches. Conventional evaluation relies on annotation-intensive reference standards and incomplete structured data, limiting population-scale use. We propose a multi-stage validation framework for LLM-based clinical information extraction that enables rigorous assessment under weak supervision by integrating complementary validation strategies. The framework combines prompt calibration, rule-based filtering, semantic grounding, judge-LLM evaluation, expert review, and predictive validity analysis to quantify uncertainty without exhaustive manual annotation. We applied this framework to extract substance use disorder (SUD) diagnoses across 11 substance categories from 919,783 clinical notes. Rule-based filtering and semantic grounding removed 14.59% of LLM-positive extractions that were unsupported or structurally implausible. For high-uncertainty cases, the judge LLM showed substantial agreement with subject matter expert. Using judge evaluations as references, the primary LLM achieved an F1 score of 0.80. LLM-extracted SUD diagnoses predicted subsequent engagement in SUD specialty care more accurately than structured-data baselines. By unifying complementary validation strategies, this work presents a generalizable human-in-the-loop framework for establishing the trustworthiness of LLM-based clinical information extraction at scale while minimizing the need for exhaustive manual annotation.

title: Deep learning super-resolution enhances MRI radiomics for predicting placenta accreta spectrum and invasiveness.
desc: [European journal of radiology] Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS) is a severe obstetric complication. This study evaluated whether retrospective, post-processing deep learning-based super-resolution reconstruction (SR) was associated with improved MRI radiomics performance for predicting PAS and invasive PAS. This retrospective study involved 245 patients who had placental MRI scans at three different institutions. Of these, 158 cases from Institution I for training set and internal validation set, while 34 patients from Institution II and 53 patients from Institution III served as external validation sets. SR using a generative adversarial network (GAN) was applied to generate SR T2WI (SRT2WI). Predictive models for PAS and invasive PAS were developed based on T2WI, SRT2WI, and the SRT2WI-Clinical model. Two radiologists independently diagnosed PAS using T2WI to serve as a reference for evaluating model performance. Model performance was assessed using the area under the curve (AUC), calibration curves, decision curve analysis (DCA), Delong test, and net reclassification improvement (NRI). SHAP values interpreted the models and quantified feature contributions. Across all four cohorts, SRT2WI yielded numerically higher AUCs than T2WI, and SRT2WI-Clinical achieved the highest AUCs. For PAS, SRT2WI-Clinical achieved AUCs of 0.953, 0.887, 0.793, and 0.788 in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts 1 and 2, respectively (T2WI: 0.738, 0.697, 0.654, and 0.652; SRT2WI: 0.879, 0.820, 0.696, and 0.768). Corresponding AUCs for invasive PAS were 0.895, 0.875, 0.843, and 0.815 (T2WI: 0.774, 0.699, 0.575, and 0.745; SRT2WI: 0.861, 0.794, 0.729, and 0.808). For PAS, SRT2WI-Clinical significantly outperformed T2WI (P < 0.001) and SRT2WI (P = 0.004) only in training, with no significant validation differences. For invasive PAS, it significantly outperformed T2WI in training, internal validation, and external validation cohort 1 (P = 0.003, 0.021, and 0.019, respectively), but not external validation cohort 2 (P = 0.398); comparisons with SRT2WI were nonsignificant. Calibration showed good agreement, DCA favored SRT2WI-Clinical, and SHAP quantified feature contributions. The combination of SR and radiomics shows promise for improving the prediction of PAS and invasive PAS. Integrating clinical features may further enhance model performance, supporting its potential clinical utility.

title: Houston Methodist tackles ambient AI in surgery
第三届精神领域学科融合与创新大会举行 重医附一院与京东健康共建“心理康复与医疗智能体实验室”
Large language models for depression assessment from brief daily diaries
desc: Closely tracking changes in depression is important for clinical research and practice. However, intensive longitudinal depression assessment relies on self-report surveys that have major limitations. Scoring depression from natural language with large language models (LLMs) could resolve these shortcomings. This study tested the validity of depression rated by LLMs from daily video diaries. We studied 108 participants selected for mental health treatment status (45% in treatment). Participants completed a clinical interview and 14-21 days of depression surveys and video diaries. Daily depression scores were estimated by LLMs from diary transcripts. LLM ratings converged with self-report depression within-person ( r = .45;95% CrI[.40, .49]) and when averaged across days for an overall depression score ( r = .61;95% CrI[.43,.75]). Averaged LLM ratings correlated with depression symptom severity ascertained by clinical interview ( r = .53;95% CrI[.35, .68]). LLM-rated depression and self-report had similar profiles of associations with daily functioning variables (profile r = .98 within-person; r = .94 between-person). Multivariable regression results showed LLM ratings predicted daily functioning variables (partial $$\beta s$$ β s =|.12 | - | .28 | ) and interview-rated depression (partial $$\beta$$ β =.33;95% CrI[.07, .58]) over and above self-reports, suggesting LLMs capture clinically-relevant information that self-reports miss. Findings establish a strong foundation for a depression assessment approach that addresses shortcomings of self-reports while satisfying the unique demands of intensive longitudinal monitoring.

title: Accuracy, Usefulness, and Expert-Perceived Clinical Impact of Response Variability in ChatGPT-4o for Hyperlipidemia-Related Questions.
desc: [Journal of pharmacy practice] ChatGPT-4o, an advanced Artificial Intelligence based large language model, has demonstrated utility for providing medical information. Data regarding its accuracy and usefulness for hyperlipidemia pharmacotherapy are limited. Additionally, the clinical implications of variability in responses generated from simultaneous identical prompts across multiple sessions remains poorly understood. This research aimed to (1) assess accuracy, (2) evaluate usefulness, and (3) examine perceived impact variability of ChatGPT-4o generated responses to hyperlipidemia-related clinical questions. Five questions addressing hyperlipidemia management and patient counseling were developed. Responses to the questions were collected simultaneously from three independent ChatGPT-4o sessions initiated in separate, newly opened ChatGPT windows. A modified Delphi technique using clinical pharmacy faculty evaluated responses for accuracy, usefulness, and impact variability. Scores were evaluated using a 3-point Likert scale. After initial scoring, responses were collected, collated, and redistributed to faculty for review and optional revision. Final evaluations and consensus were facilitated by a moderator during a virtual panel. Consensus was reached for all responses. Evaluations of response accuracy ranged from poor to good, while usefulness ranged between somewhat useful and very useful. Impact variability ranged from none to high across responses, which faculty concluded could impact patient management. Response variability may have potential clinical implications; however, the present study evaluated expert-perceived potential impact rather than actual patient outcomes. Users should be aware concurrently generated ChatGPT responses can differ in accuracy and usefulness. Clinical judgment and patient-centered multidisciplinary collaboration remain essential. Future directions include using a larger data set to corroborate findings.

title: As measles outbreak surges, AI can forecast hotspots
GWDRO-Lung: Gromov–Wasserstein distributionally robust learning for calibrated pulmonary nodule malignancy prediction across imaging cohorts
desc: Low-dose chest computed tomography (CT) screening detects pulmonary nodules whose malignancy risk must be triaged, yet deep-learning risk models often lose both accuracy and calibration when transferred to a different scanner, protocol, or population. We developed GWDRO-Lung, a chest CT framework that treats cross-cohort transfer as a coupled problem of structural mismatch, distributional instability, and calibration. A weight-shared three-dimensional encoder with embedded acquisition metadata summarizes each cohort as a relation matrix over learned prototypes; cohort geometries are aligned to a shared Gromov–Wasserstein barycenter; and a distributionally robust, calibration-aware risk head estimates malignancy, with the residual alignment error setting a cohort-specific robustness radius. The model was developed on 1842 pulmonary nodules from LIDC-IDRI, organized into three acquisition-defined cohorts, and validated externally on 618 nodules from the independent LNDb cohort, with leave-one-cohort-out, protocol-shift, size-stratified, and decision-curve analyses. Relative to the strongest recent imaging baseline, external area under the receiver operating characteristic curve improved from 0.857 to 0.878, external expected calibration error fell from 0.106 to 0.066, worst-cohort AUC rose from 0.829 to 0.851, and net benefit was higher across triage-relevant thresholds. Prospective, pathology-confirmed validation is required before clinical use.

title: Reproductive technologies and biobanking for wild felids.
desc: [Theriogenology] The rapid decline of wild felid populations necessitates the integration of in situ and ex situ conservation strategies, aligned with sustainable development, under the One Conservation paradigm. This review examines the evolution, current applications, and future perspectives of Assisted Reproductive Technologies (ARTs), biobanking, and advanced biotechnologies in wild felids. Conventional ARTs have advanced significantly; pharmacological semen collection via urethral catheterization and laparoscopic ovum pick-up (LOPU) have emerged as highly efficient, welfare-oriented alternatives for gamete recovery. For population management, laparoscopic tubal ligation is highlighted as a safe contraceptive method that preserves ovarian function for future oocyte donation, circumventing the severe pathologies associated with long-term hormonal implants. Beyond conventional ARTs, cutting-edge strategies such as somatic cell nuclear transfer (SCNT) and the xenotransplantation of gonadal and post-mortem somatic tissues provide critical avenues for rescuing lost genetics from highly valuable individuals. Furthermore, the logistical and analytical bottlenecks of genetic resource banks are being addressed through next-generation biobanking. The paradigm shift toward Predictive Andrology, driven by Artificial Intelligence (AI), enables the accurate forecasting of semen cryotolerance using multi-dimensional biological and environmental data. In conclusion, the synergistic integration of modernized ARTs, advanced tissue biobanking, and AI-driven predictive models is indispensable for safeguarding the felid genomic reservoir and ensuring their long-term survival.

title: Lab to codes: multimodel advanced AI-driven pipelines to drive antimicrobial peptide design for the post-antibiotic era.
source: PubMed · Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
desc: [Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology] The rapid emergence of global antimicrobial resistance (AMR) has outpaced the development of new antimicrobial agents, necessitating transformative approaches such as AI-driven in-silico drug discovery. Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are promising alternatives due to their broad-spectrum bactericidal activity and limited susceptibility to resistance. However, the transition from bench to bedside remains constrained by certain challenges, such as instability, potency, and cytotoxicity. Here, well-integrated, multi-model AI-driven pipeline strategies for the mining and discovery of novel AMPs are designed to address these concerns through simultaneous multi-purpose optimization. The proposed architectural frameworks combine discriminative AMP classifiers, quantitative potency, and cytotoxicity screening filters to prioritize AMPs with good efficacy and safety profiles. To ensure novelty, the pipeline integrates multi-layer sequential and genomic screening by adopting alignment and profile-based approaches. Structural refinements are achieved through advanced molecular docking (MD) and protein folding approaches, providing mechanistic insights regarding peptide-target interactions. In parallel, enzymatic susceptibility and stability prediction models are incorporated to optimize AMP pharmacokinetic potentials. Notably, the multi-objective pipeline operates within iterative optimization loops; discriminative and generative AI models and sequential redesign strategies refine candidates based on multi-purpose closed feedback loops across stability, novelty, efficacy, and toxicity outcomes. These systematic and integrated approaches overcome key bottlenecks associated with traditional linear drug discovery, potentially reducing late-stage attrition and accelerating the transformation from in-silico predictions to wet-lab validation. Collectively, this review provides reproducible and generalizable blueprints for next-generation antimicrobial agents, demonstrating the computational potentials of AI-driven, multi-model architectural frameworks to tackle the global AMR crisis and favour precision design of AMPs with better therapeutic indices.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Early Prediction of Intracranial Hypertension: From Single-Centre Development to Multicentre Validation.
desc: [Neurocritical care] Raised intracranial pressure is one of the most severe secondary insults after traumatic brain injury. Recognising physiological patterns before they progress to dangerous intracranial pressure elevations could enable preventive rather than reactive interventions. In our previous Uppsala single-centre study, an XGBoost machine learning model showed high discriminative performance for prediction of imminent intracranial pressure insults. The model identifies short-term physiological trajectories associated with imminent threshold crossing rather than predicting independent future clinical events. Whether these results are generalisable across centres is unknown. The aim was therefore to evaluate whether the XGBoost model trained on an Uppsala dataset maintains similar performance when applied to a multicentre TBI cohort - The CENTER-TBI High-Resolution ICU cohort. The XGBoost model trained on the Uppsala high frequency traumatic brain injury cohort was externally validated using data from the multicentre CENTER-TBI cohort. Minute-level averages of intracranial pressure and invasive arterial blood pressure were used to predict the onset of an intracranial pressure insult within 30 min on the basis of a 4h historical window. A bidirectional validation design was applied and performance was assessed using multiple metrics. The cohorts comprised 602 patients from Uppsala and 255 patients from the CENTER-TBI database. When trained on the Uppsala cohort and tested on CENTER-TBI, the model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 97.4%, sensitivity of 93.8%, and specificity of 98.6%. Training on CENTER-TBI and testing on the Uppsala dataset yielded an AUROC of 96.1%, sensitivity of 81.2%, and specificity of 98.7%. Balanced accuracy exceeded 88% in both validation directions. The XGBoost model retained high performance under external multicentre validation, indicating that pre-insult physiological patterns preceding increased intracranial pressure are shared across cohorts. Differences in sensitivity between validation directions were observed and may reflect cohort characteristics or dataset size. These findings support the need for local evaluation before clinical implementation.

title: Gut microbiota-cancer crosstalk: emerging molecular targets for personalized cancer treatment- a comprehensive review.
desc: [Frontiers in molecular biosciences] Cancer remains a major global health challenge, and growing evidence indicates that the gut microbiota plays an important role in cancer initiation, progression, metastasis, and response to treatment through complex interactions with host signaling, metabolism, and immunity. This comprehensive narrative review discusses the molecular mechanisms underlying gut microbiota-cancer crosstalk, with particular emphasis on dysbiosis, microbial metabolites, immune modulation, and microbiota-regulated oncogenic pathways, including TLR/NF-κB, Wnt/β-catenin, JAK/STAT, PI3K/Akt/mTOR, and Hippo-YAP signaling. The review also examines emerging molecular targets, including microbial extracellular vesicles, bacterial small RNAs, ferroptosis-related mechanisms, and microbiota-mitochondria interactions. In addition, current microbiota-targeted therapeutic strategies, such as fecal microbiota transplantation, engineered bacterial therapeutics, CRISPR-based microbiome engineering, and microbiome-informed approaches to precision oncology are discussed. Relevant peer-reviewed literature published primarily within the recent 5-year period was considered from major scientific databases and publisher platforms, including PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Springer, Elsevier, and MDPI. Overall, the available evidence suggests that gut microbiota represents an important component of the tumor ecosystem and may provide promising biomarkers and therapeutic targets. Integration of microbiome research with multi-omics and artificial intelligence may further support the development of personalized cancer treatment.

title: The Biomarker Revolution in Kidney Transplantation.
desc: [Journal of clinical medicine] Since the first successful kidney transplant in 1954, transplant medicine has advanced significantly, achieving favorable one-year outcomes. However, despite excellent short-term outcomes, long-term renal allograft survival remains sub-optimal, with acute rejection continuing to be a major contributor to death-censored allograft loss. Current approaches for post-transplant surveillance and rejection monitoring rely on either nonspecific markers that often detect injury late in their course or invasive procedures associated with procedural risks and complications. To address these limitations, numerous non-invasive biomarkers have been introduced into solid organ transplantation research with the goal of improving allograft surveillance, facilitating earlier detection of rejection and complementing existing diagnostic approaches. Although several biomarkers have demonstrated clinical promise, none currently possess sufficient accuracy to replace kidney allograft biopsy. Biomarkers under investigation include blood-, tissue- and urine-based specimens. Their development and validation as independent markers have been limited by smaller sample size, heterogenous targets, variable performance characteristics and suboptimal sensitivity and specificity. In response, the field has increasingly shifted toward multimodal approaches that combine biomarkers and incorporate artificial intelligence to improve diagnostic accuracy and outcomes prediction. This review summarizes current biomarkers, discusses their limitations and explores future directions for biomarker development and clinical implementation.

title: The promise and perils of artificial intelligence in molecular biology.
desc: [Molecular cell] In this Voices article, six investigators reflect on the growing role of artificial intelligence (AI) in molecular biology research. They discuss AI's potential to accelerate discovery, enhance data analysis, and generate new hypotheses, while also highlighting challenges related to reliability, bias, reproducibility, and the need for human oversight.

title: From smart sensing to adaptive remediation: artificial intelligence and Internet of Things for persistent organic pollutants.
desc: [Environmental monitoring and assessment] Persistent organic pollutants (POPs) remain a major environmental challenge because of their persistence, long-range transport, bioaccumulation, and resistance to degradation. Conventional monitoring and remediation systems provide reliable analytical performance but are largely fragmented, laboratory dependent, and unable to deliver the continuous, predictive, and adaptive management required for complex, dynamic contamination scenarios. Recent literature reports substantial advances in biosensors, Internet of Things (IoT)-enabled sensing, machine learning (ML), and artificial intelligence (AI) for pollutant detection, forecasting, source identification, and remediation optimization. However, these developments often operate separately, with limited coordination between environmental sensing, data analytics, treatment processes, and decision-making. The literature further highlights persistent barriers to field deployment, including limited and geographically heterogeneous datasets, inconsistent sensor performance and calibration, restricted model transferability, insufficient independent validation, uncertainty in AI predictions, and the lack of mature regulatory frameworks for AI-assisted environmental assessment. From our perspective, the next advance in POP management should move beyond isolated AI applications toward integrated, closed-loop AI-IoT architectures that continuously connect sensing, prediction, remediation, and feedback control. Such systems could transform POP management from reactive assessment to proactive and adaptive environmental governance. Future progress will depend on standardized, Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable (FAIR) environmental datasets, explainable and uncertainty-aware AI, robust field validation, and interoperable sensing infrastructures.

title: Correlative SEM-AFM Characterization of 2D Materials: From Sequential Measurements to In-Situ Multimodal Platforms.
desc: [Nanomaterials (Basel, Switzerland)] With atomic-scale thickness and defect-sensitive structures, stimuli-responsive two-dimensional (2D) materials exhibit diversified and highly localized physicochemical behaviors under external triggers such as electric fields, illumination, mechanical strain and chemical environments. These behaviors are intricately coupled with layer variations, grain boundaries, folds and local strain fields, which makes it necessary to reveal the structure-performance relationships of stimuli-responsive 2D materials. Compared with conventional single-technique characterization, the combination of scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and atomic force microscopy (AFM) provides a powerful framework for correlating structural, morphological and functional information across length scales. In this review, a systematic overview of correlative and integrated SEM-AFM characterization of 2D materials is given, covering its origins, working principles, typical applications and recent progress. Representative measurement configurations are classified into three categories-sequential SEM and AFM characterization, integrated AFM-in-SEM platforms, and truly in-situ or simultaneous SEM-AFM measurements-and the corresponding applications to stimuli-responsive 2D materials are discussed with respect to electrical, optical, mechanical and multiphysics characterization. The experimental challenges and limitations of SEM-AFM integration, including electron-beam effects, contamination, vacuum constraints and drift-related issues, are critically analyzed. Finally, the development of intelligent SEM-AFM platforms accompanied by emerging deep learning and artificial intelligence (AI) paradigms is outlined as a perspective, with emphasis on multimodal data fusion and automated feature extraction.

title: HIP: Hessian Interatomic Potentials without derivatives.
desc: [Nature computational science] Molecular Hessians, the second derivatives of the potential energy, are fundamental to many workflows in computational chemistry. Usually, accurate Hessians are computationally expensive to calculate and scale poorly with system size, whether computed using quantum chemistry methods or machine learning interatomic potentials. Here we introduce Hessian Interatomic Potentials (HIPs), a deep learning model that directly predicts Hessians without relying on automatic differentiation or finite differences. To do so, we construct SE(3)-equivariant, symmetric Hessians from irreducible representation (irrep) features up to degree l = 2, computed by a graph neural network. HIP Hessians are one to two orders of magnitude faster, more accurate, more memory efficient, easier to train and exhibit favorable scaling with system size. We validate our predictions across a wide range of downstream tasks, demonstrating consistently superior performance in transition state search, geometry optimization, zero-point energy corrections and vibrational analysis. We open source the HIP code and model weights.

title: Red Blood Cells Beyond Oxygen Transport: Dynamic Regulators, Disease Biomarkers and Therapeutic Platforms-A Narrative Review.
source: PubMed · International journal of molecular sciences
desc: [International journal of molecular sciences] Red blood cells (RBCs) have traditionally been regarded as passive carriers of respiratory gases. Increasing evidence, however, indicates that they are active participants in vascular homeostasis and respond to mechanical, metabolic, and oxidative stimuli. This narrative review examines the interconnected roles of RBCs as regulators of vascular physiology, indicators of hereditary and systemic disease, therapeutic targets, and delivery platforms. RBC deformability, membrane organization, ion-water balance, metabolism, and redox capacity support microcirculatory flow, while ATP release, nitric oxide handling, adhesion, and extracellular-vesicle formation influence vascular function. RBC morphology, mechanics, hydration, metabolism, oxidative status, and vesiculation can provide clinically relevant information, although emerging functional and molecular biomarkers require further standardization and validation. RBC-directed treatments and RBC-based carriers offer additional therapeutic opportunities. Automated image analysis and machine-learning-assisted microfluidic classification are the most substantiated artificial-intelligence applications; broader multimodal decision-support systems remain exploratory.

title: Multichannel Polysomnographic Sensor Fusion for Automatic Sleep Stage Classification.
desc: [Sensors (Basel, Switzerland)] Automatic sleep stage classification can reduce the burden of manual polysomnographic scoring, but reliable models must account for heterogeneous physiological signals, temporal dependencies, and severe class imbalance. This study presents a dual-stream deep learning framework for five-class sleep staging from 30 s polysomnographic segments using two EEG signals, one EOG signal, and one submental EMG signal. Time-domain features are extracted through one-dimensional convolutions, while complementary time-frequency information is obtained from short-time Fourier transform spectrograms processed by a two-dimensional convolutional branch. The resulting features are fused and analyzed over a five-segment context window using a bidirectional long short-term memory network. Prolonged wake periods are censored only during training to reduce majority-class dominance without altering the evaluation distribution. Subject-wise five-fold cross-validation across 78 subjects yielded a mean accuracy of 91.5%, a balanced accuracy of 78.5%, a macro-F1 score of 77.4%, and a Cohen's kappa of 0.829. Controlled architectural and channel-ablation experiments further quantified the contributions of temporal context, time-frequency processing, wake censoring, and the individual PSG signals. A lightweight time-domain-only variant achieved 88.8% accuracy, 72.7% balanced accuracy, a macro-F1 score of 73.8%, and a Cohen's kappa of 0.779. These findings support the use of multimodal time-frequency fusion for robust automatic sleep staging while highlighting the trade-off between classification performance and model complexity.
